title: A yearly retreat
hook: a few days of silence each year
tomorrow: Sofia's back from retreat with a fever. is God mad at her?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: once a year, the same road, a different you. Today the road ends somewhere quiet.

Three days, no phone, the permission slip says. Hand it in at the door. To some people that sounds like rest; to others, a sentence. Why would anyone choose silence on purpose, once a year? No scrolling, no group chat, nothing to show for it on Monday. Jesus's friends got that invitation first, on a day so crowded they hadn't eaten.
screen: `THREE DAYS, NO PHONE.` → `REST, OR A SENTENCE?` → `WHY CHOOSE SILENCE?`

segments.voice: In Mark, the apostles come back from their first mission full of stories, and so many people are coming and going that they have no time even to eat. Jesus says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Come apart into a desert place, and rest a little." Apart, not away for good. One to tell a friend: they take a boat to the quiet place, and the crowd runs ahead and beats them there. Jesus has compassion and teaches them anyway. Even the first retreat got interrupted. That's the Catholic retreat: a few days of silence and prayer, often with a guide, so you come back with your attention handed back to you. Saint Ignatius of Loyola wrote his Spiritual Exercises as a guide for that kind of time, and retreats are still built on them. A neighbor tradition says it too, and far more often. Jews who keep the Sabbath stop every week. In the Jewish Publication Society's 1917 translation of the commandments: "Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy." What's shared: stopping is holy. Rest isn't time stolen from God; it's kept for God. And an honest difference: for Jews who keep it, the Sabbath is a commandment, every week, kept at home and with the community. A Catholic retreat is chosen, and might come once a year, usually away from home.
screen: `COME APART, AND REST A LITTLE.` · `THE CROWD GOT THERE FIRST.` · `THE SPIRITUAL EXERCISES.` · `REMEMBER THE SABBATH DAY.` · then, large: `A FEW DAYS APART.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes, or rest them on the floor. For these two minutes you're on a very small retreat: no phone, no task, nobody to answer. When a thought pulls at you, let it wait on the far shore. If you pray, you can hear the line again: come apart, and rest a little.
A yearly retreat. A few days of silence and prayer, chosen on purpose, so you return to the crowd rested. Today's word.
Hold on to this: a few days apart, so you can come back. Rest well.

screen: `DAY 1700 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: BACK FROM RETREAT WITH A FEVER. IS GOD MAD?`

howItsDone: Catholics make retreats at retreat houses, monasteries or parishes, from a weekend to several days, often in silence and with a director; schools and parishes run retreats for students and families.
